title: Candidate handshake: technical sandbox & access protocol
content:
Purpose:
Small pragmatic proto for how we hand a candidate (offer accepted -> first release) a low-friction technical sandbox, access checklist, and an interviewer/mentor pairing protocol. Goal is to reduce first-week friction, shorten time-to-first-meaningful-contribution, and provide consistent signals for managers and interviewers.

Context & why this exists:
- We get repeated slowdowns from candidates waiting on account provisioning, repo access, infra creds, and ambiguous onboarding tasks.
- Engineering managers want predictable ramp metrics (first PR, infra test pass, small customer-facing change).
- Interviewers want consistent evidence: did candidate complete guided sandbox, can they run CI locally, do they follow contributor norms?

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) After acceptance HR sends the handshake packet (links + high-level timeline).
2) People Ops triggers a sandbox provision job (cloud dev instance + guided exercise + ephemeral dataset).
3) Candidate gets 48hr window to try sandbox pre-boarding (opt-in).
4) On day 0 manager assigned a mentor + 2-step access checklist is executed.
5) First 14 days use micro-credential tasks to validate environment and reduce support load.

Preboarding sandbox (opt-in):
- What we provide: ephemeral cloud dev instance (4GB RAM, 2 vCPU), curated repo fork with a single-ticket guided issue, a small synthetic dataset (anonymized), and a runbook PDF.
- Why: lets candidate validate their dev environment, try a Redwood-specific inference microflow, and surface OS/SSH/browser issues early.
- Security note: sandbox is isolated, timeboxed (48–72 hours), and audited; no production keys included.

Technical exercise (guided):
- Step 0: read runbook.md (10–15 mins).
- Step 1: clone the fork, run the unit smoke test (./scripts/smoke.sh).
- Step 2: implement a tiny change (add a logging tag to the inference client) and open a PR to their fork.
- Step 3: run the local integration (docker compose limited stack) and upload the test result artifact.
- Deliverable: PR link + test artifact + 1–3 lines summary of hurdles.

Access & provisioning checklist (day 0 owner: People Ops -> infra):
- [ ] ID verification & paperwork complete (People Ops)
- [ ] SSO account created (SCIM + Okta)
- [ ] GitHub org invite sent and accepted (teams: eng/<pod>, infra-read)
- [ ] Internal wiki access (read) + onboarding-runbook page assigned
- [ ] CI token (read-only) created and stored in vault; ephemeral creds used for sandbox only
- [ ] Slack workspace invite + #pod-channel added + buddy ping scheduled
- [ ] Local dev secrets doc shared (minimal, no prod keys)
- [ ] Hardware voucher request (if remote in region) or laptop imaging slot scheduled
- [ ] Health & payroll tasks completed (people-ops)

Interviewer / Mentor pairing protocol (for hiring loops & new joiners):
- Pairing ladder: mentor (day-to-day onboarding) + interviewer buddy (first 90d touchpoint).
- Interviewer expectations aligned with rubric below before any technical debriefs.
- Mentor to run a 30-minute "environment check" within 48 hours of access completion.

Interview rubric (lightweight, used for calibration & new-interviewer training):
- Repo hygiene (did candidate run the smoke test without hand-holding?) -> Evidence: pass/fail + notes
- Debugging fluency (how did candidate triage failing step?) -> Evidence: 1–3 line summary in PR
- Code style & simplicity -> Evidence: PR diff + reviewer notes
- Operational awareness (containerize/run locally) -> Evidence: artifact upload + log snippet
- Communication & async notes -> Evidence: summary lines + Slack thread behavior if sandbox used
- Scorecards: A/B/C where A: minimal guidance, completes all steps; B: completes with small hints; C: needs heavy hand-holding or infra blockers

First 14-day micro-credential slate (manager & mentor checkpoints):
- Day 1: environment validated (mentor sign-off).
- Day 3: make a small noncritical PR and get feedback.
- Day 7: run a smoke pipeline end-to-end and interpret logs.
- Day 10: shadow an oncall/playbook run or run a small customer-facing debug flow.
- Day 14: demo first-14-day deliverable (screen share 15 mins) to manager + mentor.

Manager signals we track (minimal, practical):
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (target < 7 days)
- Time-to-local-smoke-pass (target < 3 days)
- Number of infra access escalations (target 0–1)
- Candidate/employee reported friction score (0–5) after day 7

Owner responsibilities (who does what):
- People Ops: kick sandbox job, verify paperwork, monitor voucher/inventory
- Infra: create ephemeral sandbox, ensure logging and audit trail, help with CI tokens
- Eng manager: assign mentor, review micro-credential slate, evaluate day-14 deliverable
- Mentor: run env check, triage access blockers, daily 30-min sync for first 5 days

Open questions & TODOs (working list):
- Should sandbox include a short recorded walkthrough video? (Priya working on a script)
- Do we provide a local VM image vs cloud ephemeral instance (cost tradeoff)? (Infra to recommend)
- Need legal sign-off for synthetic dataset distribution across regions (Dmitri)
- Automate pass/fail artifact capture into a hiring metadata bucket (JIRA ticket: JIRA-HR-402)

Edge cases & mitigation notes:
- Candidate with strict corporate VPN: provide browser-based cloud IDE to avoid local VPN conflicts.
- Accessibility needs: provide alternate formats for runbook, extended sandbox time on request, earmark mentor bandwidth.
- International hires where hardware shipping delayed: prioritize cloud-only workflows for first 14 days.

Short checklist for hiring coordinators (practical):
- 24–48h preboarding email with links + opt-in sandbox toggle
- Confirm Okta invite + GitHub invite accepted before day 0
- Confirm mentor assigned and calendar scheduled

How to use this doc (process):
- People Ops: copy runbook template from /onboard-templates/sandbox and tailor to pod
- Infra: use infra/team-library/sandbox-provision script and tag PR with 'sandbox-ready'
- Hiring manager: confirm micro-credential slate in the offer packet and include mentor name

Appendix (links & templates):
- runbook template: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-templates/runbook-sandbox.md
- email template: confluence://people-ops/email-templates/acceptance-handshake
- checklist script: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/team-library/sandbox-provision

Notes to self (sticky reminders):
- Keep the sandbox exercise intentionally small (20–45 mins active) but value-packed.
- Track analytics for 3 months and iterate: acceptance -> sandbox opt-in rate, infra ticket volume, time-to-first-PR.
- Prioritize mentor availability in offer negotiation for high-skill roles.
